scope: Section-entry regression checks include 42 empty and 42 populated section/width combinations selected by real desktop or mobile navigation clicks from deep scroll, an overview visible only in Analysis, section-specific entry headings, a visibly rendered save-state label in every section at all widths with a separate single live announcement, Evaluation isolated from audit records and available without a project, and 14 real keyboard Home/End selections with mobile Escape dismissal. Count-card text contrast is sampled while Analysis is rendered. These extend the retained workflows: Local interface-phase checks with an explicitly selected headless QA profile. Sidebar workspace with rendered Cinnabar navigation, burnt orange selected tabs and primary actions, cream navigation text and dark text on a pale warm locality note, slate body text, neutral canvas and white paper surfaces, vertical desktop and mobile tab orientation, responsive two-column and single-column control cards with visible claim bindings and readable body text, long-token control-name wrapping with original project restoration, complete canonical project summary visibility, exact navigation breakpoint checks at 760 and 761 pixels, actual record counts, search and combined claim/class/evidence-state filters with reset preservation, scientific result and audit bindings, explicit execution-target selection, selection retention across unrelated renders and errors, no automatic target after planning, disabled unavailable execution actions, keyboard tabs, focusable panels, deep-scroll section navigation, visible failed-action feedback, one accessible save-status live region checked through the Chrome accessibility tree across responsive widths, destination focus after candidate, source-review and annotation workbenches open, mobile focus boundaries, file menus, reduced motion, text-only rendering, unsaved input protection and reversion, prepared downloads, cancelled and coherent project replacement, complete workspace reset, candidate, source and multi-case annotation draft protection, programmatic field tracking, procedure-specific fields, exact-byte UTF-8/BOM input inspection, reference and paired execution, explicit bootstrap coverage/seed recording, linked responsive reports and print styles, description drafting, candidate editing, multi-claim, unassessed evaluation, blank judgment workbench, visible review headings, and review archive roundtrip. Evaluation snapshot hashes and bundle/partition invalidation, pending-input locking and failure recovery, stale-session renewal without automatic replay, a named outbound-preview dialog with initial Cancel focus and button/native-Escape cancellation, and a mocked interrupted hosted-request response are included. Dialog previews use fixed synthetic local mocked responses without any provider transmission. All computations and edited inputs were hypothetical software fixtures. Recorded public identity metadata was used only to display the source-review form; no human source review or benchmark judgment was submitted, and no external page request was observed. Targeted small-text pairs, real hovered navigation label and count pairs, focused tab, brand and mobile close outlines, and the mobile close icon have contrast ratios computed from rendered styles; this does not assess every visual state. This is browser integration coverage, not a screen-reader, full accessibility, print-pagination, or scientific validation. Audit-remediation checks exercise real-key Not judged, explicit Uncertain and partial-dimension choices, four synthetic DEVELOPMENT_FIXTURE submissions through the actual local annotation API, imported assessed nulls, retained evidence predictions, revision chains, and backend agreement calculated from the workbench-generated sheets. Their required human_attested booleans are synthetic contract fixtures and do not represent human benchmark or source review. The first two sheets yield two paired labels and kappa 0; explicit uncertainty yields three paired labels and kappa 0.5. The decorative breadcrumb is ignored in the accessibility tree and its rendered contrast is included. Browser process exit, when a verified PID is supplied, is measured separately from endpoint refusal.
